name: The Anomaly Observatory — Infrastructure Comparator Casebook
purpose: Historical source-linked exemplars of material infrastructure disruptions, NOT a census, representative sample, or trend estimator.
selection: Selected public, source-backed incidents with material disruption to essential services or major shared infrastructure; one incident per upstream failure where known.
baseRateWarning: Do not calculate a monthly/annual rate or claim acceleration from these curated records. Use consistently collected population-level datasets for event-frequency testing.

benchmarks.label: Data-center outage frequency per site
benchmarks.scope: Per-site outages in Uptime Institute research
benchmarks.caveat: Does not describe every cloud, aviation, banking or public-sector outage.

benchmarks.label: Severity of major publicly reported outages
benchmarks.finding: Higher impact in 2024 than earlier years
benchmarks.scope: Publicly reported major outages tracked by Uptime
benchmarks.caveat: Selected major media-reported outages, not an unbiased census of all failures.

benchmarks.label: Dependence on third-party providers
benchmarks.finding: Roughly two-thirds of tracked public outages involve third-party providers
benchmarks.caveat: A share of observed outages, not an annual growth rate or a probability of cascading failure.

events.title: Southwest holiday network collapse
events.metric_note: Cancellations across the 2022 Christmas–New Year disruption; the displayed date is illustrative of this multi-day event, not a precise onset.
events.cause: Severe winter weather and Southwest operational recovery limitations
events.note: DOT reports over 2 million stranded passengers.

events.title: FAA NOTAM system failure and ground stop
events.cause: NOTAM system malfunction and recovery errors
events.note: A historically relevant comparator to the November 2026 FAA ground stop.

events.title: AT&T national wireless disruption
events.metric_note: FCC reported more than 92 million calls blocked, including over 25,000 attempted 911 calls.
events.note: Affected voice, data and access to emergency calling for at least 12 hours.

events.title: Change Healthcare payment-system cyberattack
events.metric_note: No standardized count of interrupted transactions used.
events.note: Cross-organization dependence on a healthcare payment and claims intermediary.

events.title: CrowdStrike faulty-update disruption
events.metric_note: Microsoft estimate of devices affected; not an incident count.
events.note: One shared software dependency disrupted organizations in many sectors.

events.title: Spain–Portugal power system blackout
events.metric_note: Geographic characterization, not a count of customers.
events.note: Energy-sector comparator showing infrastructure failures are not confined to software.

events.title: AWS Northern Virginia regional incident
events.metric_note: Downstream customer numbers not established consistently.
events.cause: DNS-related failures and cascading service dependencies
events.note: An example of several business disruptions arising from one upstream incident.

events.title: Cloudflare network disruption
events.cause: Configuration/data-handling failure as described in provider postmortem
events.note: A single platform incident with broad downstream effects.

events.title: Microsoft 365 service disruption
events.metric_note: No defensible unique-customer magnitude at publication.
events.cause: Latent software defect, changed traffic, reduced gateway capacity
events.note: Reportedly involved shared network gateways used by Outlook and other Microsoft services.

events.title: FAA communications failure and national ground stop
events.metric_note: FAA reports cancellations on the day; not all directly attributable to the ground stop.
events.note: A useful matched reference class exists in the January 2023 FAA event.

events.title: United Airlines internal system interruption
events.metric_note: Reported service disruption duration; not a passenger estimate.
events.cause: Internal system failure; no reported evidence of cyberattack
events.note: Counted separately from the FAA incident because it was an independent internal incident.
